authoredFrom: The 400-file corpus draw found a module-less file — otp/lib/syntax_tools/examples/merl/basic_test.erl, whose -module line is COMMENTED OUT because the file is included into another module. Erlang has no way to name such a file, so the file path is the only identity available and it is what the members are owned by. Writing a module symbol for it would fabricate a module that does not exist, and dropping the members would lose four real function definitions. The analyzer chose the path; the independent oracle initially chose nothing, which lost the ownership entirely — that is the adjudication this fixture records. The fixture deliberately carries no -export: OTP's own merl fragment does (`-export([basic_fib/1])`), but pinning that here would make the fixture depend on a change in the shared fixture runner, which is committed separately. The owner fallback is the subject, and it needs no harness change.

expectSymbols.name: fragment_helper
expectSymbols.note: owned by the FILE PATH: the file declares no -module, so the path is the only identity it has (ER-D32). Its -export is still a top-level, importable unit - a file-scope unit in the harness's own terms.

expectSymbols.name: FRAGMENT_MACRO
expectSymbols.note: owned by the FILE PATH too. The 400-file draw caught macros taking bare ctx.moduleName while functions/records/types/callbacks took the path fallback, so a macro in a module-less file had NO owner while the function beside it had one.
